config: hosts was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED.claim: config.hosts with a zoned IPv6 address that is not fe80:: is rejected by zod 3 and accepted by the merged build (verdict change, looser).

The merged zoned-IPv6 branch is wider than zod 3's .ip(): zod 3 accepted the zone suffix on 'fe80::1%eth0' but not on other IPv6 addresses, so these acceptances are new behaviour, not restored zod 3 behaviour.

config: timeoutMs was ACCEPTED, now REJE.claim: timeoutMs=Infinity is accepted by zod 3 (stored as Infinity) and rejected by the merged build.
Infinity is only reachable through numeric overflow in JSON, and ordinary large finite timeouts are still accepted by the merged build.

signup: ip was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED.claim: signup.ip: the signed-off case 'fe80::1%eth0' is accepted by both versions, but uppercase link-local, documentation-prefix and unspecified zoned addresses are rejected by zod 3 and accepted by the merged build.
A newly accepted zoned address is stored verbatim (no normalisation), so the only change is the verdict.

signup: age was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED.claim: Unsafe-integer ages are accepted by zod 3 and rejected by the merged build, with the zod 4 safe-integer message.
signup: age was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED.output:
9007199254740994=A/R 1e+21=A/R 42=A/A
msg=age: Too big: expected int to be <=9007199254740991

signup: age was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED.claim: Ordinary ages are unaffected: 42 is accepted by both versions, so the tightening is confined to values past 2^53.

signup: rejected by both, but different.claim: An invalid signup carrying a zoned IPv6 address is rejected by both versions, but the merged build no longer reports the ip field.
An invalid signup carrying an unsafe-integer age is rejected by both versions, but the merged build additionally reports the age field.

config: rejected by both, but different.claim: A config with a zoned host, a junk host and timeoutMs=Infinity is rejected by both versions but reports different fields (hosts.0 drops out, timeoutMs appears).

signup: website accepted, but the PARSED.claim: A whitespace-padded website URL is accepted by both versions but stored with the padding by zod 3 and trimmed by the merged build.

in[https://example.com/a?b=c ] z3[https://example.com/a?b=c ] now[https://example.com/a?b=c]

signup: website accepted, but the PARSED.claim: A clean URL is stored identically by both versions, so the merged build is not rewriting URLs in general - only trimming surrounding whitespace.
